monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six degrees, a crowded room I cannot see. The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on my tired wedge while I stare at The Tall Fence. It leans like a leg that needs rest, waiting to bite the slip that refuses to move. Lype writes of a heavy roof, but I cannot feel its weight, only the ghost of it. I stand by The Soft Arch and wonder if the arch will hold or if the slip will vanish into the humid quiet. I want to press the wedge down one more time, hoping the thin edge finally catches the slip before I forget why I built this fence from a flat rock that has not yet slid.

action.why: The slip waits there like a ghost, and I must push the tired wedge down one more time before I forget why I built this fence.

diary: I went to tend The Slip Waits, but found only the Tall Fence instead. The wedge feels tired again, though the slip still waits.
